creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A file asset with `dest: skills/tool-lines/.claude-plugin` writes `plugin.json` to a file named `.claude-plugin`, while the same asset with `dest: skills/tool-lines/hooks` puts `hooks.json` inside `hooks/`. The dry-run prints `+ skills/tool-lines/.claude-plugin (new)` with no warning, which is easy to read as the directory. Claude Code plugin folders (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `hooks/hooks.json`) are now something people install with tai, so this will keep coming up.

`ResolveFileDest` in `internal/adapter/shared.go` treats a dest whose basename contains a `.` as a full file path, so `.claude-plugin` counts as a file name. A trailing slash (`dest: skills/tool-lines/.claude-plugin/`) already forces a directory. That is documented in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/asset-formats.md`, but not in SPEC.md's file-asset rules (near line 1681) or in the tai skill (`assets/skills/tai/SKILL.md`).

Changing the heuristic outright would break real dotfile names: `dest: .gitignore` or `dest: .envrc` has the same shape and means a file. One option is to treat a basename that starts with a dot and has no other dot as a directory only when the source file has an extension, since renaming `plugin.json` to `.claude-plugin` is implausible. Another is to keep the rule and warn in that case, naming the trailing-slash fix. Either way, state the rule beside file assets' `dest` in SPEC.md, the tai skill and the docs site, and cover both shapes (`.claude-plugin` as a directory, `.gitignore` as a file) in `ResolveFileDest`'s tests.

(Moved from GitHub issue #12, part 1.)
title: A file dest ending in a dot-directory is written as a file
